subject: Zipline MAP: hosting verification sprint & final regional decision
messages:
From: Olivia Rivera <olivia@zipline.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Jacob Song <jacob.song@zipline.ai>
Date: 2026-07-26T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: MAP sprint and region preference for hosting

Karthik —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Zipline is aligned to move into a 2-week verification sprint inside the MAP, and we want to lock the hosting mode + primary region for testing so we can staff the right infra and security reviewers. Quick context: our compliance team prefers not to go fully hosted for anything more than PoC, but product engineering wants the fastest path to low latency in the US East region.

Could you confirm:
- Rough delta in timeline if we choose Hosted (fastest) vs Dedicated (predictable throughput) vs Private (on-prem/VPC)?
- What artifacts you can provide up-front for security reviewers (SOC2 evidence, network diagrams, data flow)?

We aim to sign a short SOW by Aug 6 and start canary tests Aug 10. If that timeline is unrealistic for any hosting mode, let us know.

Attaching the MAP draft we mentioned.

—Olivia
Zipline, Sr. PM

Attachment: zipline_MAP_v3.pdf

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Rivera <olivia@zipline.ai>, Jacob Song <jacob.song@zipline.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-26T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP sprint and region preference for hosting

Hi Olivia — thanks for the clear summary. High-level answers below; I also pasted a proposed short-run timeline at the bottom for the MAP sprint.

Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (very brief):
- Hosted: quickest to start (1–2 business days to spin test model in hosted stack once we sign SOW), best TTV, fallback paths available. Good if you want to assess feature quality quickly.
- Dedicated: ~2–3 weeks to provision and validate capacity (GPU pools, autoscaling policy). Predictable throughput/cost, recommended if you expect sustained production traffic during the pilot.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): 4–8 weeks depending on network approvals and on-prem packaging. Best for regulated data flow and strict KMS/HSM requirements.

Security artifacts we can provide now: SOC2 summary, architecture diagram, data flow spreadsheet, keys & encryption whitepaper. Lauren will attach the checklist items.

Proposed MAP sprint (suggested):
- Week 1 (Aug 10–14): Hosted proof-of-quality in us-east (fastest path). Red flags/acceptance tests run.
- Week 2 (Aug 17–21): If performance gating passes, parallel Dedicated provisioning begins for a canary (if you want predictable load).
- Aug 24: Decision checkpoint — go-live path chosen (Hosted or Dedicated) or extend to Private runway if compliance is blocking.

If Zipline prefers to rule out Hosted entirely up-front, we should start Dedicated provisioning immediately — that adds the 2–3 week window.

Next steps: I’ll drop the security artifacts and a short hosting tradeoffs doc. Can we schedule a 45-min sprint kickoff tomorrow to align on acceptance tests?

Thanks,
Karthik
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: hosting_tradeoffs.md

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Olivia Rivera <olivia@zipline.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-26T13:48:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP sprint and region preference for hosting

Olivia / team — adding the security lens here. A few quick clarifications for Zipline's compliance reviewers: 

- For Hosted: we can provide a compact SOC2 artifact bundle (control summaries + evidence pointers) within 48 hours of the kickoff. We can also provide per-route token-level logs and retention policies.
- For Dedicated: we expose audit logs, tenant isolation diagrams and can integrate with customer KMS (bring-your-own-key) — usually a + for procurement.
- For Private: we surface an on-prem checklist (network ACLs, HSM/KMS integration steps) but it does require your infra team to run the on-prem package validation.

One litmus test: if Zipline requires HSM-backed signing inside your VPC for inference, that pushes strongly towards Private. If the ask is "customer-controlled KMS in cloud", Dedicated covers it.

I attached a security_summary.xlsx with the control checkpoints and the minimum artifacts procurement will request.

—Lauren
Senior Security PM, Redwood Inference

Attachment: security_summary.xlsx

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Olivia Rivera <olivia@zipline.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-27T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP sprint and region preference for hosting

Looping in timeline and SOW coordination. Procurement at Zipline indicated they need a one-page SOW by next Friday (Aug 6) and a pricing anchor for Dedicated (monthly commit + burst). Jacob — can you confirm the expected concurrency for the canary so we can size dedicated pools?

Internally: if we go Hosted first, we should still prepare a Dedicated quote in parallel (fast path: estimate based on 10–50 concurrent requests; adjust at checkpoint). Stephanie, can you draft the SOW (one-pager) and share a quick pricing matrix?

Thanks — Marissa
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

Attachment referenced: SOW_draft.docx

From: Jacob Song <jacob.song@zipline.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Olivia Rivera <olivia@zipline.ai>, Procurement Team <procure@zipline.ai>
Date: 2026-07-27T11:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP sprint and region preference for hosting

Thanks Marissa — for the canary we expect roughly 30 concurrent inference sessions for a two-hour peak window (internal estimate). If Dedicated is sized for 50 concurrent, that gives us headroom.

Procurement note: we prefer a short-term Dedicated pilot with the option to convert to reserved capacity. Sending this note to procure@zipline.ai to formalize the SOW request. Also, compliance asked for the SOC2 evidence bundle ASAP.

—Jacob
Product Ops, Zipline

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Rivera <olivia@zipline.ai>, Jacob Song <jacob.song@zipline.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-28T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP sprint and region preference for hosting

Excellent — thanks everyone for the fast responses. Quick summary / agreed next steps: 

1) Timeline: We’ll proceed with Hosted proof-of-quality in us-east for Week of Aug 10 (start Aug 10). If acceptance tests pass at the Aug 24 checkpoint, we’ll either keep Hosted or enable Dedicated canary provisioned in parallel. Dedicated sizing initial anchor: 50 concurrent for canary (per Jacob).
2) Security artifacts: Lauren will drop the SOC2 summary + security_summary.xlsx today. Zipline procurement will get the one-page SOW from Stephanie by COB Jul 30.
3) Procurement & SOW: Marissa will lead SOW reviews; Zipline Proc (procure@zipline.ai) will confirm signature path and if they need a PO before canary.
4) Acceptance tests: Olivia will share the short acceptance checklist by Monday (Aug 3). Redwood will publish a short playbook for canary test harness and rollback conditions.

Attachments delivered: hosting_tradeoffs.md, security_summary.xlsx, SOW_draft.docx, zipline_MAP_v3.pdf (link in Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1Zp-line-MAP-v3)

If nothing else, I’ll schedule the 45-min kickoff tomorrow 10:00am PT (invite to follow).

—Karthik
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
